transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to address the twenty-four drums of solvent waste from the recent line-cleaning operation that are currently secured in the hazardous-waste cage. As you know, the temporary storage permit for those drums expires on Friday, so we need to move forward with disposition. Before I can record any disposition decision, I'll need both Jon and Priya to present the current information: Jon, I'll need the laboratory results and waste-log information for these drums; and Priya, I'll need the current batch-genealogy and hold information. Once we have those records in front of us, we can complete the two-part review and determine whether these drums meet the approved recovery specification for solvent recovery, or if they'll need documented treatment instead. Let's get started whenever you're ready.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I received the laboratory classification report yesterday. Fifteen drums meet the approved solvent-recovery specification, three drums fail the water-content limit and must go to hazardous-waste incineration, and the remaining six drums were not classified in that report. A laboratory-system outage has kept the report from being uploaded to the waste log, so the waste log doesn't reflect these results yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: My completed batch-genealogy review identifies the 6 unclassified drums as drums from lot VX-204, which contain residual catalyst and must be retained on site for exactly 30 days for possible process investigation rather than sent for treatment. The hold tags have not yet been entered in the production system.
transcript.speaker: A3
